resolution.title: Let a grid status menu show past the scrolling table
resolution.description: The order status menu in the Orders list is cut off when the list is short. The grid is wrapped in a `.table-responsive` (`Grid/Blocks/table.html.twig`), which Bootstrap defines as:  `.table-responsive { display: block; width: 100%; overflow-x: auto; }`  Once one axis is not `visible`, CSS makes the other one clip as well, so the container clips vertically even though only horizontal scrolling was asked for. With a few orders the table is only a couple of rows high, the status menu is taller than that, and the part that does not fit is cut - which is what the screenshot in the report shows.  The horizontal scrolling is still wanted for wide grids, so instead of dropping it the container is allowed to overflow only while a menu is open, and put back when it closes. It is scoped to the grid's own choice menus, so no other dropdown behaviour changes.  `data-boundary` was not the answer here: it changes where Popper positions the menu, not whether an ancestor clips it, so the menu would still have been cut.
resolution.how_to_test: Sell > Orders with only a few orders in the list, so the table is short. Open the status menu on a row: before this change the entries that do not fit inside the table are cut off; after it, the whole menu is visible and the table still scrolls horizontally when it is too wide.
resolution.author: boo-code

ticket.title: Carrier::getDeliveredCountries() uses wrong states ID resulting in wrong countries list
ticket.bug:
The new getDeliveredCountries() code has an error when fetching active states linked to delivered countries.
This is because when using the $countries array in `array_keys($countries)` its keys are in numeric order starting from 0, not using id_country as keys.
$countries has no id_country as keys. $result has them.
So `SELECT` is using `IN (0,1,2,3,....)` instead of correct country ids. This results in wrong countries list with countries without carries in it.
https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/25f0ef48696506fcee01e34de069d0c7a3b7c144/classes/Carrier.php#L670
ticket.expected: Correct country list with ONLY countries with a carrier enabled.
ticket.steps: Just call the Carrier::getDeliveredCountries() function. You'll also get countries for which there aren't carriers available. For better proof, disable carriers for the countries with low states ID in them (like 0,1,2,3,4). They will be included anyway for the error explained in description.

resolution.title: Fix states lookup using row indexes instead of country IDs
resolution.description: `Carrier::getDeliveredCountries()` builds its states sub-query from `array_keys($countries)`, but `$countries` is the raw `executeS()` result with numeric row indexes (0, 1, 2, …) — not country IDs. Only `$result` is keyed by `id_country`. As a consequence, states of unrelated countries are fetched, and the line `$result[$state['id_country']]['states'][] = $state` silently auto-creates malformed entries containing only a `states` key (no `id_country`, no `name`). When `PS_RESTRICT_DELIVERED_COUNTRIES` is enabled, `CustomerAddressFormatter::getFormat()` iterates this array and emits `Undefined array key "id_country"` / `"name"` warnings (CustomerAddressFormatter.php:100-101), and the FO address form's country dropdown contains broken/extra entries. This PR uses `array_keys($result)` instead, so only states of actually delivered countries are fetched and no phantom entries can be created. Regression introduced in #40044 (shipped since 9.0.2).
resolution.how_to_test: 1. In the BO, go to International > Locations > Countries and enable "Restrict country selections in front office to those covered by active carriers" (`PS_RESTRICT_DELIVERED_COUNTRIES`). 2. Make sure at least one country with a **low ID** and active states (e.g. enable a country whose `id_country` is below the number of delivered countries) is active but **not** covered by any active carrier. 3. In the FO, open the address creation form (My account > Addresses > Create new address). Before the fix: PHP warnings `Undefined array key "id_country"` / `"name"` from `CustomerAddressFormatter.php:100-101` in the logs, and broken/unexpected entries in the country dropdown. After the fix: no warnings, the dropdown lists only carrier-covered countries, and their states load correctly.
resolution.author: paulschwahn

ticket.title: Changing an order's status throws "Duplicate entry '<idp>-<idpa>-0-0' for product_sqlstock" when the order contains a deleted combination (single-shop)
ticket.bug:
On a **single-shop** install (no multistore, no stock sharing, `share_stock = 0`), changing an order's status fails with:

```
[PrestaShopException code 23000] : SQLSTATE[23000]: Integrity constraint violation: 1062 Duplicate entry '14-183-0-0' for key 'ps_stock_available.product_sqlstock'
```

The error is order-specific: some orders move to the new status fine, others always fail.

**Root cause (investigated):** the failing order contains a **product combination that was later deleted**. `order_detail` still references the old `id_product_attribute` (e.g. `183`), but that combination no longer exists in `product_attribute` / `product_attribute_shop`. When the new status updates stock, `StockManager::getStockAvailableByProduct()` / `StockAvailable::setQuantity()` cannot resolve a shop context for the dead combination and writes a `stock_available` row with `id_shop = 0, id_shop_group = 0`. On a single-shop store this `0-0` row is invalid (it should be `id_shop = 1`). The first qualifying order creates that orphan row; any later order referencing the same deleted combination then collides on the `product_sqlstock` unique key.

Still present (verified in source) in **8.2.6** and **9.1.3**: in `src/Adapter/StockManager::getStockAvailableByProduct()`, when `$id_shop === null` and stock is not shared, `$stockAvailable->id_shop = (int) $id_shop;` evaluates to `0`.
ticket.expected: Changing an order's status should not fail when an order line references a combination that has since been deleted. A `stock_available` row should never be written with `id_shop = 0` on a single-shop install.
ticket.steps:
1. Single-shop install (no multistore).
2. Create a product with a combination (e.g. weight "100 g") → `id_product_attribute = A`.
3. Place an order containing that combination (`order_detail.product_attribute_id = A`).
4. Delete combination `A` from the product (e.g. replace it with another weight).
5. Set that order to a status that updates stock (e.g. "Delivered"). → A `stock_available` row `(product, A, 0, 0)` gets created; this order succeeds.
6. Set another order that also contains combination `A` to that status. → `Duplicate entry '<product>-A-0-0' for key 'product_sqlstock'`.

resolution.title: Fix:  Changing an order's status throws "Duplicate entry '<idp>-<idpa>-0-0' for product_sqlstock" when the order contains a deleted combination (single-shop)
resolution.description: This PR prevents stock movement creation for deleted product combinations by stopping `prepareMovement()` when `productAttributeId > 0` and the related combination no longer exists, using an adapter to avoid direct legacy usage in Core, preventing unintended `stock_available` recreation during order status changes and duplicate key errors.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Single-shop install (no multistore).  Create a product with a combination (e.g. weight "100 g") → id_product_attribute = A.2.   3. Place an order containing that combination (order_detail.product_attribute_id = A).  4. Delete combination A from the product (e.g. replace it with another weight).  5. Set that order to a status that updates stock (e.g. "Delivered"). → The order status is updated successfully and no stock_available row (product, A, 0, 0) is created.  6. Set another order that also contains combination A to that status. → The order status is updated successfully, no duplicate entry error is thrown, and no stock_available row is recreated for the deleted combination.
resolution.author: Codencode

resolution.title: Fix multilang fallback for fields using isRequiredWhenActive and defaultLanguageRequiredWhenActive validators
resolution.description: When a multilang field uses the `isRequiredWhenActive` or `defaultLanguageRequiredWhenActive` validator instead of `required => true`, the fallback mechanism in `ObjectModel::formatFields()` was skipped. This caused non-default languages to be saved as empty strings in the database instead of inheriting the default language value. The CartRule `name` field was changed from `required => true` to `required => false` with `validate => defaultLanguageRequiredWhenActive` in a previous commit (8d3da9f5d6). This broke the fallback, causing blank promo names in FO, exceptions at checkout, and missing order statuses when using a non-default language. The fix extends the fallback condition in `ObjectModel::formatFields()` to also trigger for these two validators, which are semantically equivalent to `required` for the default language value. A Behat regression test is also added to cover this scenario.

Check the `ps_cart_rule_lang` table: the `name` column for FR must contain the EN value, not an empty string. 6. In FO, add a product to cart, switch to FR, apply the promo code → the discount name must appear correctly and checkout must complete without exception. resolution.title: Cart rule compatibility search does not filter results for new cart rule
resolution.description: When editing the "Compatibility with other cart rules" autocomplete (Catalog → Discounts → Cart Rules → tab *Conditions* → "Compatible with other cart rules"), the search field does not filter the list of cart rules. Typing a search term still returns all cart rules instead of those matching the term. This happens whenever the cart rule has no compatibility restriction set yet - i.e. when **creating a new cart rule** (`id_cart_rule=0`) or editing an existing one whose `cart_rule_restriction = 0`.  Root cause: in `CartRule::getAssociatedRestrictions()`, when `!Validate::isLoadedObject($this) \|\| $this->cart_rule_restriction == 0`, the method runs an SQL query that **never applies** the `$search_cart_rule_name` argument. The `LIKE` filter only exists in the other branch, through `getCartRuleCombinations()`, which is reached only for an already-saved rule with `cart_rule_restriction = 1`.  Fix: apply the missing `AND tl.name LIKE "%...%"` filter (escaped via `pSQL()`) in that branch, only for the `cart_rule` type and only when a search term is provided.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Go to **Catalog → Discounts** and create a few cart rules with distinct names (e.g. `10% off`, `-50% summer`, `Free shipping`). 2. Type part of a name (e.g. `10`). **Before:** the list ignores the term and shows all cart rules. **After:** the list is filtered to cart rules whose name matches the term. 4. Repeat while editing an existing cart rule that has its compatibility restriction disabled - same result.

ticket.title: Invalid product URLs trigger Fatal in ProductController::assignPriceAndTax (PHP 8 / PS 9)
ticket.bug:
`ProductController::initContent()` unconditionally calls `assignPriceAndTax()` without checking whether `$this->product` is a loaded object. When the product cannot be loaded (deleted, inactive, invalid id in the URL), `init()` already
 handled the case by setting the 404 template and returning , but `Controller::run()` keeps going and calls `initContent()` anyway, leading to a Fatal error.

**Call chain:**
```
Controller::run() [classes/controller/Controller.php:308]
  → ProductController::initContent() [controllers/front/ProductController.php:306]
    → ProductController::assignPriceAndTax() [line 529]
       → crash on line 536 (getTaxesRate on null) OR line 539 (getPriceStatic with null id)
```

**Two observable crash points:**

- `ProductController.php:536` , `$this->product->getTaxesRate(...)` → Fatal `Call to a member function getTaxesRate() on null` when `$this->product === null` (URL has `id_product=0` or missing id).
- `ProductController.php:539` , `Product::getPriceStatic($this->product->id, ...)` → `PrestaShopException('Product ID is invalid.')` when `$this->product` is a non-loaded Product object (`new Product(XXXXX)` where the id doesn't exist
returns an object with `id = null`).

**Why `init()` doesn't prevent it:** `init()` correctly detects the invalid product (line 133) and calls `setTemplate('errors/404'); return;`, but the `return` only exits `init()`, not `run()`. `Controller::run()` proceeds to call
`initContent()` regardless.

**Why this is a PHP 8 regression:** PS 1.7 / PS 8 `ProductController` had the same logical flaw, but PHP 7 tolerated `null->method()` with a silent warning. PHP 8 turns it into a `TypeError`.

**Real-world impact:** on any production store with indexed URLs, search engine crawlers (Google, Bing, Facebook) continuously hit URLs of deleted/renamed products. On our store (540k orders, 50k+ products, multilingual) this produces
~40 `*ERROR* Product ID is invalid` entries per hour in `var/logs/<YYYYMMDD>_exception.log`, plus occasional 500s in Apache error log. Zero functional impact (caught exceptions are silenced upstream for most code paths), but the log
noise drowns out legitimate errors.
ticket.expected: A request to a non-existent or deleted product URL should return HTTP 404 rendered via the `errors/404` template that `init()` already selected, with no Fatal error, no PrestaShopException, and no entry in `exception.log`.
ticket.steps:
1. On any PS 9 install, hit a URL of a non-existent or deleted product, e.g.:
   ```
   https://<shop>/<lang>/999999-nonexistent.html
   https://<shop>/<lang>/<id_of_deleted_product>-<old-slug>.html
   ```
2. Browser receives `HTTP 500`.
3. Check `var/logs/<YYYYMMDD>_exception.log` and `/var/log/apache2/error.log`:
   - `PHP Fatal error: Uncaught Error: Call to a member function getTaxesRate() on null in controllers/front/ProductController.php:536`
   - And/or `*ERROR* Product ID is invalid. at line 3363 in file classes/Product.php`
4. Stack trace consistently terminates at `ProductController::assignPriceAndTax()` → `initContent()` → `Controller::run()`.

resolution.title: Guard product page when product is null
resolution.description: This PR adds a null guard around product-dependent logic in `ProductController` to avoid errors when the product is not available or not properly initialized. It ensures methods like `initContent()` and breadcrumb generation do not try to access product data when `$this->product` is `null`, making the product page flow more robust in invalid or edge-case contexts.

ticket.title: CountryQueryBuilder::getCountQueryBuilder() always returns 1 instead of the true total
ticket.bug:
`CountryQueryBuilder::getCountQueryBuilder()` always returns `1` as the country count, regardless of how many countries exist in the database.

The root cause is that `->groupBy('c.id_country')` is placed in the shared `getQueryBuilder()` method (`src/Core/Grid/Query/CountryQueryBuilder.php`, line 106), which is called by **both** `getSearchQueryBuilder()` and `getCountQueryBuilder()`. The count query therefore inherits `GROUP BY`, becoming:

```sql
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.id_country)
FROM ps_country c
INNER JOIN ps_country_lang cl ON cl.id_country = c.id_country AND cl.id_lang = 1
INNER JOIN ps_zone z ON z.id_zone = c.id_zone
INNER JOIN ps_country_shop cs ON c.id_country = cs.id_country AND cs.id_shop IN (1)
GROUP BY c.id_country;
```

This returns one row per country, each with value `1`. `DoctrineGridDataFactory::fetchOne()` picks the first row → the total is always `1`.
ticket.expected: `getCountQueryBuilder()` should return a single row with the true total number of countries (e.g. `241`), so that any consumer of `DoctrineGridDataFactory` with the country grid receives the correct `totalItems`.
ticket.steps:
1. Install PrestaShop with the default country dataset.
2. Run the following SQL against your database (replace `id_lang` and `id_shop` with your actual values):

```sql
-- Find your values:
SELECT id_lang FROM ps_lang WHERE active = 1 LIMIT 1;
SELECT id_shop FROM ps_shop WHERE active = 1 LIMIT 1;

-- Buggy count query (as generated by getCountQueryBuilder):
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.id_country)
FROM ps_country c
INNER JOIN ps_country_lang cl ON cl.id_country = c.id_country AND cl.id_lang = 1
INNER JOIN ps_zone z ON z.id_zone = c.id_zone
INNER JOIN ps_country_shop cs ON c.id_country = cs.id_country AND cs.id_shop IN (1)
GROUP BY c.id_country;
```

3. Observe that the query returns **241 rows, each containing `1`**, instead of a single row with `241`.
4. Confirm by inspecting `CountryQueryBuilder::getCountQueryBuilder()` in `src/Core/Grid/Query/CountryQueryBuilder.php` — `groupBy('c.id_country')` is inherited from `getQueryBuilder()`.

resolution.title: Fix: CountryQueryBuilder::getCountQueryBuilder() always returns 1 instead of the true total
resolution.description: This PR fixes the country grid total count calculation. `CountryQueryBuilder::getCountQueryBuilder()` was reusing a base query that already contained `GROUP BY c.id_country`, causing the count query to return multiple rows with value `1` instead of a single row with the real total. The `GROUP BY` is now applied only to the search query, while the count query keeps using `COUNT(DISTINCT c.id_country)` without grouping.  This keeps the country list deduplicated in multistore contexts and restores the correct `totalItems` value for the grid.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Enable the experimental **"Countries"** feature in **Advanced Parameters > New & Experimental Features**. 2. Go to **International > Locations > Countries**. 3. Check that the total displayed in the table header matches the actual number of countries and is **not `1`**.
resolution.author: Codencode

ticket.bug:
Updating a logo, mail logo or invoice in multistore with single shop selected causes TypeError with PHP 8.3 and crashes.

_ShopCore::getGroupIdFromShopId(): Argument #1 ($shopId) must be of type int, null given, called in ../prestashop/classes/shop/Shop.php on line 1015_

`\PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Core\Shop\LogoUploader::updateInMultiShopContext` also makes couple of calls `Shop::setContext(Shop::CONTEXT_GROUP);` without second `$id` argument that is also available in the same function. Therefore that is probably not working as intended and might cause some issues, but I didn't get in that deep.

ticket.title: Bug: reserved_quantity not updated when "Share available quantities for sale" is enabled (Multishop)
ticket.bug:
In a multishop environment with 2 shops in the same shop group, when the option:

**Shop Group → Share available quantities for sale**

is enabled (`true`),

product quantities are shared between shops.

However, when placing an order, the system does not correctly update the `reserved_quantity` field in the `stock_available` table.

This happens because in this situation, the `stock_available` records have `id_shop = 0`, but the `PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Adapter::updateReservedProductQuantity()` method performs the update by passing `id_shop = ID_SHOP` (e.g., `id_shop = 1`). Therefore, the query does not match any row in stock_available.

As a result, `reserved_quantity` is never updated.

When the order status changes to **Shipped**: `physical_quantity` is never recalculated correctly.
ticket.steps:
- Enable multishop.
- Create a shop group with:
  - 2 shops
  - "Share available quantities for sale" = true
-  Create a product with stock.
- Place an order in one shop.
-  Check the `stock_available` table and verify that the `reserved_quantity` field has not changed (it remains 0), while it should be updated with the purchased quantity.

resolution.title: Fix: Bug: reserved_quantity not updated when "Share available quantities for sale" is enabled (Multishop)
resolution.description: When multishop is enabled and "Share available quantities for sale" is set to true, the stock_available row is stored with id_shop = 0.  However, `updateReservedProductQuantity()` was using the current shop ID, causing the UPDATE query to not match any row. This resulted in reserved_quantity not being updated and `physical_quantity` never being recalculated properly. This fix resolves the correct stock shop ID (0 when `share_stock `is enabled) before executing the update query.
resolution.how_to_test: TEST 1 - Enable multishop. - Create a shop group with: 2 shops and shop group with field **Share available quantities for sale** = true - Create a product with stock. - Place an order in one shop. - Check the `stock_available` table and verify that the `reserved_quantity` field has been updated with the purchased quantity. - Change the order status to "Shipped" and verify that the `physical_quantity` field has been updated accordingly. TEST 2 - Create 2 shop groups, each with 2 shops and with field **Share available quantities for sale** = true. - Create a product with stock assigned to both shop groups. - Place an order in one shop of the first group and verify that `reserved_quantity` is updated only for that shop group (id_shop = 0 within the group scope). - Ensure that stock values of the second shop group remain unchanged.
resolution.author: Codencode

ticket.title: Cart rule combinations lost when saving if lazy-loaded list (jscroll) is not fully loaded
ticket.bug:
When editing a cart rule with a large number of “compatible cart rules”, the Back Office loads the list using *infinite scroll* (`jscroll`), but **only the currently loaded items are included in the `<select name="cart_rule_select[]>` POST payload**.

Because of this, when saving a cart rule **without scrolling the list to the end**, PrestaShop deletes *all* existing combinations for that rule (as part of the normal `afterUpdate` process), then recreates them only from the partial list sent in the form.

This leads to **data loss**: most combinations disappear permanently after the user saves the rule.

This affects both:

- existing combinations loaded from DB,
- new combinations added via AJAX,
- any combinations not currently loaded in the DOM at save time.

This is a **core data integrity bug** caused by BO lazy-loading in file [conditions.tpl](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/65e40453e0478cf5472093b69ae567d0d2b5d6b4/admin-dev/themes/default/template/controllers/cart_rules/conditions.tpl#L271) + how PrestaShop reconstructs cart rule combinations after update.
ticket.expected:
Saving a cart rule **should not delete combinations that were not visible in the DOM** due to lazy-loading.

Either:

- the UI should send **all existing combination IDs**, not only loaded items,  
**or**
- the backend should preserve existing combinations instead of deleting them blindly.
ticket.steps:
1. Create a large number of cart rules (e.g. 1000+).
2. Edit any cart rule that has many combinable rules.
3. In the “Conditions” tab, the list of combinable rules is rendered using `jscroll` and loads items in batches via AJAX infinite scroll.
4. Do **not** scroll to the bottom — leave most combinations not loaded.
5. Click **Save**.
6. PrestaShop removes all combinations:
   ```sql
   DELETE FROM cart_rule_combination 
   WHERE id_cart_rule_1 = X OR id_cart_rule_2 = X
   ```
7. PrestaShop recreates combinations only from:
   ```
   POST['cart_rule_select[]']
   ```
   — which contains **only the few rules loaded at the top**.
8. The majority of combinations are lost.

resolution.title: Fix: Cart rule combinations lost when saving if lazy-loaded list (jscroll) is not fully loaded
resolution.description: This PR fixes how cart rule combinations are saved when using an AJAX-loaded select. Previously only the options loaded in the dropdown were considered, so combinations could be incomplete if the user didn’t scroll the list. The form now submits the list of unselected cart rules, and the backend derives the selected ones from the full set, ensuring all intended combinations are stored correctly.

The grid is wrapped in a `.table-responsive` (`Grid/Blocks/table.html.twig`), which Bootstrap defines as:  `.table-responsive { display: block; width: 100%; overflow-x: auto; }`  Once one axis is not `visible`, CSS makes the other one clip as well, so the container clips vertically even though only horizontal scrolling was asked for. With a few orders the table is only a couple of rows high, the status menu is taller than that, and the part that does not fit is cut - which is what the screenshot in the report shows. It is scoped to the grid's own choice menus, so no other dropdown behaviour changes.  `data-boundary` was not the answer here: it changes where Popper positions the menu, not whether an ancestor clips it, so the menu would still have been cut.

ticket.title: Carrier::getDeliveredCountries() uses wrong states ID resulting in wrong countries list
ticket.bug:
The new getDeliveredCountries() code has an error when fetching active states linked to delivered countries.
This is because when using the $countries array in `array_keys($countries)` its keys are in numeric order starting from 0, not using id_country as keys.
$countries has no id_country as keys. $result has them.
So `SELECT` is using `IN (0,1,2,3,....)` instead of correct country ids. This results in wrong countries list with countries without carries in it.
https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/25f0ef48696506fcee01e34de069d0c7a3b7c144/classes/Carrier.php#L670
ticket.expected: Correct country list with ONLY countries with a carrier enabled.
ticket.steps: Just call the Carrier::getDeliveredCountries() function. You'll also get countries for which there aren't carriers available. For better proof, disable carriers for the countries with low states ID in them (like 0,1,2,3,4). They will be included anyway for the error explained in description.

resolution.title: Fix states lookup using row indexes instead of country IDs
resolution.description: `Carrier::getDeliveredCountries()` builds its states sub-query from `array_keys($countries)`, but `$countries` is the raw `executeS()` result with numeric row indexes (0, 1, 2, …) — not country IDs. Only `$result` is keyed by `id_country`. As a consequence, states of unrelated countries are fetched, and the line `$result[$state['id_country']]['states'][] = $state` silently auto-creates malformed entries containing only a `states` key (no `id_country`, no `name`). When `PS_RESTRICT_DELIVERED_COUNTRIES` is enabled, `CustomerAddressFormatter::getFormat()` iterates this array and emits `Undefined array key "id_country"` / `"name"` warnings (CustomerAddressFormatter.php:100-101), and the FO address form's country dropdown contains broken/extra entries. This PR uses `array_keys($result)` instead, so only states of actually delivered countries are fetched and no phantom entries can be created. Regression introduced in #40044 (shipped since 9.0.2).
resolution.how_to_test: 1. In the BO, go to International > Locations > Countries and enable "Restrict country selections in front office to those covered by active carriers" (`PS_RESTRICT_DELIVERED_COUNTRIES`). 2. Make sure at least one country with a **low ID** and active states (e.g. enable a country whose `id_country` is below the number of delivered countries) is active but **not** covered by any active carrier. 3. In the FO, open the address creation form (My account > Addresses > Create new address). Before the fix: PHP warnings `Undefined array key "id_country"` / `"name"` from `CustomerAddressFormatter.php:100-101` in the logs, and broken/unexpected entries in the country dropdown. After the fix: no warnings, the dropdown lists only carrier-covered countries, and their states load correctly.

ticket.title: Changing an order's status throws "Duplicate entry '<idp>-<idpa>-0-0' for product_sqlstock" when the order contains a deleted combination (single-shop)
ticket.bug:
On a **single-shop** install (no multistore, no stock sharing, `share_stock = 0`), changing an order's status fails with:

```
[PrestaShopException code 23000] : SQLSTATE[23000]: Integrity constraint violation: 1062 Duplicate entry '14-183-0-0' for key 'ps_stock_available.product_sqlstock'
```

The error is order-specific: some orders move to the new status fine, others always fail.

**Root cause (investigated):** the failing order contains a **product combination that was later deleted**. `order_detail` still references the old `id_product_attribute` (e.g. `183`), but that combination no longer exists in `product_attribute` / `product_attribute_shop`. When the new status updates stock, `StockManager::getStockAvailableByProduct()` / `StockAvailable::setQuantity()` cannot resolve a shop context for the dead combination and writes a `stock_available` row with `id_shop = 0, id_shop_group = 0`. On a single-shop store this `0-0` row is invalid (it should be `id_shop = 1`). The first qualifying order creates that orphan row; any later order referencing the same deleted combination then collides on the `product_sqlstock` unique key.

Still present (verified in source) in **8.2.6** and **9.1.3**: in `src/Adapter/StockManager::getStockAvailableByProduct()`, when `$id_shop === null` and stock is not shared, `$stockAvailable->id_shop = (int) $id_shop;` evaluates to `0`.
ticket.expected: Changing an order's status should not fail when an order line references a combination that has since been deleted. A `stock_available` row should never be written with `id_shop = 0` on a single-shop install.
ticket.steps:
1. Single-shop install (no multistore).
2. Create a product with a combination (e.g. weight "100 g") → `id_product_attribute = A`.
3. Place an order containing that combination (`order_detail.product_attribute_id = A`).
4. Delete combination `A` from the product (e.g. replace it with another weight).
5. Set that order to a status that updates stock (e.g. "Delivered"). → A `stock_available` row `(product, A, 0, 0)` gets created; this order succeeds.
6. Set another order that also contains combination `A` to that status. → `Duplicate entry '<product>-A-0-0' for key 'product_sqlstock'`.

resolution.description: This PR prevents stock movement creation for deleted product combinations by stopping `prepareMovement()` when `productAttributeId > 0` and the related combination no longer exists, using an adapter to avoid direct legacy usage in Core, preventing unintended `stock_available` recreation during order status changes and duplicate key errors.

resolution.title: Fix multilang fallback for fields using isRequiredWhenActive and defaultLanguageRequiredWhenActive validators
resolution.description: When a multilang field uses the `isRequiredWhenActive` or `defaultLanguageRequiredWhenActive` validator instead of `required => true`, the fallback mechanism in `ObjectModel::formatFields()` was skipped. This caused non-default languages to be saved as empty strings in the database instead of inheriting the default language value. The CartRule `name` field was changed from `required => true` to `required => false` with `validate => defaultLanguageRequiredWhenActive` in a previous commit (8d3da9f5d6). This broke the fallback, causing blank promo names in FO, exceptions at checkout, and missing order statuses when using a non-default language. The fix extends the fallback condition in `ObjectModel::formatFields()` to also trigger for these two validators, which are semantically equivalent to `required` for the default language value. A Behat regression test is also added to cover this scenario.

Fill the name **only** in the default language (EN), set a code, enable the rule and add a reduction. 4. Save. 5. Check the `ps_cart_rule_lang` table: the `name` column for FR must contain the EN value, not an empty string. 6. In FO, add a product to cart, switch to FR, apply the promo code → the discount name must appear correctly and checkout must complete without exception. ticket.bug:
`ProductController::initContent()` unconditionally calls `assignPriceAndTax()` without checking whether `$this->product` is a loaded object. When the product cannot be loaded (deleted, inactive, invalid id in the URL), `init()` already
 handled the case by setting the 404 template and returning , but `Controller::run()` keeps going and calls `initContent()` anyway, leading to a Fatal error.

**Call chain:**
```
Controller::run() [classes/controller/Controller.php:308]
  → ProductController::initContent() [controllers/front/ProductController.php:306]
    → ProductController::assignPriceAndTax() [line 529]
       → crash on line 536 (getTaxesRate on null) OR line 539 (getPriceStatic with null id)
```

**Two observable crash points:**

- `ProductController.php:536` , `$this->product->getTaxesRate(...)` → Fatal `Call to a member function getTaxesRate() on null` when `$this->product === null` (URL has `id_product=0` or missing id).
- `ProductController.php:539` , `Product::getPriceStatic($this->product->id, ...)` → `PrestaShopException('Product ID is invalid.')` when `$this->product` is a non-loaded Product object (`new Product(XXXXX)` where the id doesn't exist
returns an object with `id = null`).

**Why `init()` doesn't prevent it:** `init()` correctly detects the invalid product (line 133) and calls `setTemplate('errors/404'); return;`, but the `return` only exits `init()`, not `run()`. `Controller::run()` proceeds to call
`initContent()` regardless.

**Why this is a PHP 8 regression:** PS 1.7 / PS 8 `ProductController` had the same logical flaw, but PHP 7 tolerated `null->method()` with a silent warning. PHP 8 turns it into a `TypeError`.

**Real-world impact:** on any production store with indexed URLs, search engine crawlers (Google, Bing, Facebook) continuously hit URLs of deleted/renamed products. On our store (540k orders, 50k+ products, multilingual) this produces
~40 `*ERROR* Product ID is invalid` entries per hour in `var/logs/<YYYYMMDD>_exception.log`, plus occasional 500s in Apache error log. Zero functional impact (caught exceptions are silenced upstream for most code paths), but the log
noise drowns out legitimate errors.
ticket.expected: A request to a non-existent or deleted product URL should return HTTP 404 rendered via the `errors/404` template that `init()` already selected, with no Fatal error, no PrestaShopException, and no entry in `exception.log`.
ticket.steps:
1. On any PS 9 install, hit a URL of a non-existent or deleted product, e.g.:
   ```
   https://<shop>/<lang>/999999-nonexistent.html
   https://<shop>/<lang>/<id_of_deleted_product>-<old-slug>.html
   ```
2. Browser receives `HTTP 500`.
3. Check `var/logs/<YYYYMMDD>_exception.log` and `/var/log/apache2/error.log`:
   - `PHP Fatal error: Uncaught Error: Call to a member function getTaxesRate() on null in controllers/front/ProductController.php:536`
   - And/or `*ERROR* Product ID is invalid. at line 3363 in file classes/Product.php`
4. Stack trace consistently terminates at `ProductController::assignPriceAndTax()` → `initContent()` → `Controller::run()`.

resolution.title: Guard product page when product is null
resolution.description: This PR adds a null guard around product-dependent logic in `ProductController` to avoid errors when the product is not available or not properly initialized. It ensures methods like `initContent()` and breadcrumb generation do not try to access product data when `$this->product` is `null`, making the product page flow more robust in invalid or edge-case contexts.

ticket.title: CountryQueryBuilder::getCountQueryBuilder() always returns 1 instead of the true total
ticket.bug:
`CountryQueryBuilder::getCountQueryBuilder()` always returns `1` as the country count, regardless of how many countries exist in the database.

The root cause is that `->groupBy('c.id_country')` is placed in the shared `getQueryBuilder()` method (`src/Core/Grid/Query/CountryQueryBuilder.php`, line 106), which is called by **both** `getSearchQueryBuilder()` and `getCountQueryBuilder()`. The count query therefore inherits `GROUP BY`, becoming:

```sql
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.id_country)
FROM ps_country c
INNER JOIN ps_country_lang cl ON cl.id_country = c.id_country AND cl.id_lang = 1
INNER JOIN ps_zone z ON z.id_zone = c.id_zone
INNER JOIN ps_country_shop cs ON c.id_country = cs.id_country AND cs.id_shop IN (1)
GROUP BY c.id_country;
```

This returns one row per country, each with value `1`. `DoctrineGridDataFactory::fetchOne()` picks the first row → the total is always `1`.
ticket.expected: `getCountQueryBuilder()` should return a single row with the true total number of countries (e.g. `241`), so that any consumer of `DoctrineGridDataFactory` with the country grid receives the correct `totalItems`.
ticket.steps:
1. Install PrestaShop with the default country dataset.
2. Run the following SQL against your database (replace `id_lang` and `id_shop` with your actual values):

```sql
-- Find your values:
SELECT id_lang FROM ps_lang WHERE active = 1 LIMIT 1;
SELECT id_shop FROM ps_shop WHERE active = 1 LIMIT 1;

-- Buggy count query (as generated by getCountQueryBuilder):
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.id_country)
FROM ps_country c
INNER JOIN ps_country_lang cl ON cl.id_country = c.id_country AND cl.id_lang = 1
INNER JOIN ps_zone z ON z.id_zone = c.id_zone
INNER JOIN ps_country_shop cs ON c.id_country = cs.id_country AND cs.id_shop IN (1)
GROUP BY c.id_country;
```

3. Observe that the query returns **241 rows, each containing `1`**, instead of a single row with `241`.
4. Confirm by inspecting `CountryQueryBuilder::getCountQueryBuilder()` in `src/Core/Grid/Query/CountryQueryBuilder.php` — `groupBy('c.id_country')` is inherited from `getQueryBuilder()`.

resolution.title: Fix: CountryQueryBuilder::getCountQueryBuilder() always returns 1 instead of the true total
resolution.description: This PR fixes the country grid total count calculation. `CountryQueryBuilder::getCountQueryBuilder()` was reusing a base query that already contained `GROUP BY c.id_country`, causing the count query to return multiple rows with value `1` instead of a single row with the real total. The `GROUP BY` is now applied only to the search query, while the count query keeps using `COUNT(DISTINCT c.id_country)` without grouping.  This keeps the country list deduplicated in multistore contexts and restores the correct `totalItems` value for the grid.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Enable the experimental **"Countries"** feature in **Advanced Parameters > New & Experimental Features**. 2. Go to **International > Locations > Countries**. 3. Check that the total displayed in the table header matches the actual number of countries and is **not `1`**.
resolution.author: Codencode

ticket.title: Uploading logo in Design -> Theme & Logo in multistore with a single shop selected causes TypeError with PHP 8.3
ticket.bug:
Updating a logo, mail logo or invoice in multistore with single shop selected causes TypeError with PHP 8.3 and crashes. 

**TypeError**
_ShopCore::getGroupIdFromShopId(): Argument #1 ($shopId) must be of type int, null given, called in ../prestashop/classes/shop/Shop.php on line 1015_

This issue also causes **ShopException** _Shop group id 0 is invalid. Shop group id must be a number that is greater than zero._



Culprit is `\PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Core\Shop\LogoUploader::updateInMultiShopContext`  that calls `Shop::setContext(Shop::CONTEXT_SHOP);` without `$idShop` as second argument even though it is readily available. Without `$idShop` `\ShopCore::setContext` tries to call `Shop::getGroupIdFromShopId($id)` with $id value of null and getGroupIdFromShopId is defined with typehint int.
I searched the project and luckily didn't find any other invalid calls to `Shop::setContext(Shop::CONTEXT_SHOP);` without Shop ID so just adding idShop as argument should be enough.

`\PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Core\Shop\LogoUploader::updateInMultiShopContext` also makes couple of calls `Shop::setContext(Shop::CONTEXT_GROUP);` without second `$id` argument that is also available in the same function. Therefore that is probably not working as intended and might cause some issues, but I didn't get in that deep.

ticket.title: Bug: reserved_quantity not updated when "Share available quantities for sale" is enabled (Multishop)
ticket.bug:
In a multishop environment with 2 shops in the same shop group, when the option:

**Shop Group → Share available quantities for sale**

is enabled (`true`),

product quantities are shared between shops.

However, when placing an order, the system does not correctly update the `reserved_quantity` field in the `stock_available` table.

This happens because in this situation, the `stock_available` records have `id_shop = 0`, but the `PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Adapter::updateReservedProductQuantity()` method performs the update by passing `id_shop = ID_SHOP` (e.g., `id_shop = 1`). Therefore, the query does not match any row in stock_available.

As a result, `reserved_quantity` is never updated.

When the order status changes to **Shipped**: `physical_quantity` is never recalculated correctly.
ticket.steps:
- Enable multishop.
- Create a shop group with:
  - 2 shops
  - "Share available quantities for sale" = true
-  Create a product with stock.
- Place an order in one shop.
-  Check the `stock_available` table and verify that the `reserved_quantity` field has not changed (it remains 0), while it should be updated with the purchased quantity.

resolution.title: Fix: Bug: reserved_quantity not updated when "Share available quantities for sale" is enabled (Multishop)
resolution.description: When multishop is enabled and "Share available quantities for sale" is set to true, the stock_available row is stored with id_shop = 0.  However, `updateReservedProductQuantity()` was using the current shop ID, causing the UPDATE query to not match any row. This resulted in reserved_quantity not being updated and `physical_quantity` never being recalculated properly. This fix resolves the correct stock shop ID (0 when `share_stock `is enabled) before executing the update query.
resolution.how_to_test: TEST 1 - Enable multishop. - Create a shop group with: 2 shops and shop group with field **Share available quantities for sale** = true - Create a product with stock. - Place an order in one shop. - Check the `stock_available` table and verify that the `reserved_quantity` field has been updated with the purchased quantity. - Change the order status to "Shipped" and verify that the `physical_quantity` field has been updated accordingly. TEST 2 - Create 2 shop groups, each with 2 shops and with field **Share available quantities for sale** = true. - Create a product with stock assigned to both shop groups. - Place an order in one shop of the first group and verify that `reserved_quantity` is updated only for that shop group (id_shop = 0 within the group scope). - Ensure that stock values of the second shop group remain unchanged.
resolution.author: Codencode

ticket.title: Cart rule combinations lost when saving if lazy-loaded list (jscroll) is not fully loaded
ticket.bug:
When editing a cart rule with a large number of “compatible cart rules”, the Back Office loads the list using *infinite scroll* (`jscroll`), but **only the currently loaded items are included in the `<select name="cart_rule_select[]>` POST payload**.

Because of this, when saving a cart rule **without scrolling the list to the end**, PrestaShop deletes *all* existing combinations for that rule (as part of the normal `afterUpdate` process), then recreates them only from the partial list sent in the form.

This leads to **data loss**: most combinations disappear permanently after the user saves the rule.

This affects both:

- existing combinations loaded from DB,
- new combinations added via AJAX,
- any combinations not currently loaded in the DOM at save time.

This is a **core data integrity bug** caused by BO lazy-loading in file [conditions.tpl](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/blob/65e40453e0478cf5472093b69ae567d0d2b5d6b4/admin-dev/themes/default/template/controllers/cart_rules/conditions.tpl#L271) + how PrestaShop reconstructs cart rule combinations after update.
ticket.expected:
Saving a cart rule **should not delete combinations that were not visible in the DOM** due to lazy-loading.

Either:

- the UI should send **all existing combination IDs**, not only loaded items,  
**or**
- the backend should preserve existing combinations instead of deleting them blindly.
ticket.steps:
1. Create a large number of cart rules (e.g. 1000+).
2. Edit any cart rule that has many combinable rules.
3. In the “Conditions” tab, the list of combinable rules is rendered using `jscroll` and loads items in batches via AJAX infinite scroll.
4. Do **not** scroll to the bottom — leave most combinations not loaded.
5. Click **Save**.
6. PrestaShop removes all combinations:
   ```sql
   DELETE FROM cart_rule_combination 
   WHERE id_cart_rule_1 = X OR id_cart_rule_2 = X
   ```
7. PrestaShop recreates combinations only from:
   ```
   POST['cart_rule_select[]']
   ```
   — which contains **only the few rules loaded at the top**.
8. The majority of combinations are lost.

resolution.title: Fix: Cart rule combinations lost when saving if lazy-loaded list (jscroll) is not fully loaded
resolution.description: This PR fixes how cart rule combinations are saved when using an AJAX-loaded select. Previously only the options loaded in the dropdown were considered, so combinations could be incomplete if the user didn’t scroll the list. The form now submits the list of unselected cart rules, and the backend derives the selected ones from the full set, ensuring all intended combinations are stored correctly.
resolution.how_to_test: 1. Create 100 cartRules (you can use this script: [createCartRules.php](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23744359/createCartRules.php))  2. Access the first created cartRule in edit mode.  3. In the **Conditions** section, select **Compatibility with other cart rules**. From the right-hand select box labeled **Combinable cart rules**, select the first 2 cartRules (without scrolling the select box) and click **Remove**. These 2 lines will appear in the left-hand select box labeled **Uncombinable cart rules**. 4. Save and remain on the page. 5. Once the page reloads, verify that the lines you previously selected are present in the **Uncombinable cart rules** section.
resolution.author: Codencode
